<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children once more; third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260513T163400-aa154244/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing child IDs, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a success. Do not mix implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260513T163400-aa154244/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

`.ddx/executions/20260513T163400-aa154244/no_changes_rationale.txt` must contain one:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` reject.

To request orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260513T163400-aa154244/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260513T163400-aa154244/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and project defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>

Power bounds remain soft scoring inputs, and exact model pins retain identity. Frontier subscription bonuses must not make power>=9 routes too attractive under default max_power=8.</context-digest>
Adjust score components so bounded default routing does not over-prefer frontier subscription routes and tests prove free-but-underpowered routes do not beat in-band routine candidates solely on cost.

Healthy power>=9 subscription bonus does not apply when effective MaxPower is below 9; default policy prefers in-band qualified candidates over materially underpowered free candidates; smart policy still allows frontier subscription/cloud routes when healthy and allowed; power scoring tests document soft undershoot/overshoot behavior

Implemented and committed as `68627584` (`fix: rebalance bounded power routing [fizeau-86b45e2c]`).

What changed:
- In [internal/routing/score.go](/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-86b45e2c-20260513T163400-aa154244/internal/routing/score.go#L16) I raised the below-min power penalty and gated the free-route bonus and the healthy high-power subscription bonus behind `candidateWithinPowerBounds`, so bounded routing does not reward underpowered or out-of-band routes just for being cheap.
- In [service_routing.go](/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-86b45e2c-20260513T163400-aa154244/service_routing.go#L215) I mirrored the stronger below-min power fit in `scorePowerHintFit` so the public evidence stays aligned with the scorer.
- In [internal/routing/score_power_test.go](/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-86b45e2c-20260513T163400-aa154244/internal/routing/score_power_test.go#L69) I added regressions proving:
  - bounded default routing prefers the in-band paid candidate over a free but underpowered local one,
  - the healthy subscription bonus is suppressed below the effective max,
  - the existing undershoot-vs-overshoot asymmetry still holds.
